assertion_analysis.fails_if: Removing the refused-index authoritative scan changes the independently counted use_index=False calls from one to zero; an added redundant scan makes it exceed one.
Keeping samples embedded prevents a separate file; the explicit direct sidecar read must increment the decode counter before its zero result is trusted.
Rebuilding during a pick yields 51 rather than the persisted 50 rows, a wrong persisted timestamp changes age=0, decoding the sidecar records a hit, and embedding samples exposes fold_inputs.

Omitting history rebuild leaves fewer than 550 rows; embedding per-run samples expands the served entry beyond 64 bytes; missing sample retention leaves the separate file below the independently generated megabyte population.

Failing to write a valid paired entry loses it or mismatches its key; retaining expired or far-future rows changes the literal count 51 or expected run-51 identity; dropping the one-hour future sample removes that identity.
An unusable cache that loses historical rows fails rows=50, and restoring unconditional authoritative scans produces a nonempty raw-call list.

A supplied-row implementation that reads ledger.runs raises the installed refusal; omitting window filtering changes the result relative to the separately read ledger profile, including the deliberately added expired and future rows.

The current assertions fail on a missing output row or on zero/multiple owner calls, but DO NOT fail if the stamp/date guards are removed because both valid folds and full rebuilds invoke the owner once with the same fixture rows; finding recorded.
Removing the leading dot in the internal filename overwrites the independently seeded other-project entry, changing its saved bytes.
Bypassing recovery fails the independently counted second index attempt or returns stale rows=50; restoring authoritative scanning makes the raw-scan predicate true.
